audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for Mahanaim, Esau messengers, Jacob's fear/prayer, gift strategy, night crossing, wrestling figure, Israel name, Peniel, and limp/hip tradition.

verses.restored: Jacob went on his way, and messengers of the Divine met him.

familiar.text: And Jacob went on his way, and the angels of God met him.

modern.text: Jacob also went on his way, and the angels of God met him.

original.text: וְיַעֲקֹ֖ב הָלַ֣ךְ לְדַרְכּ֑וֹ וַיִּפְגְּעוּ ב֖וֹ מַלְאֲכֵ֥י אֱלֹהִֽים

verses.restored: When Jacob saw them, he said, This is the camp of the Divine. He called the name of that place Mahanaim.

familiar.text: And when Jacob saw them, he said, This is God's host...

notes.title: Mahanaim
notes.body: Mahanaim means two camps or camps, matching the divine-human camp motif.

modern.text: When Jacob saw them, he said, “This is the camp of God.” So he named that place Mahanaim.

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יַעֲקֹב֙ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר רָאָ֔ם מַחֲנֵ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים זֶ֑ה וַיִּקְרָ֛א שֵֽׁם הַמָּק֥וֹם הַה֖וּא מַֽחֲנָֽיִם

verses.restored: Jacob sent messengers before him to Esau his brother, to the land of Seir, the field of Edom.

familiar.text: And Jacob sent messengers before him to Esau his brother...

modern.text: Jacob sent messengers ahead of him to his brother Esau in the land of Seir, the country of Edom.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח יַעֲקֹ֤ב מַלְאָכִים֙ לְפָנָ֔יו אֶל עֵשָׂ֖ו אָחִ֑יו אַ֥רְצָה שֵׂעִ֖יר שְׂדֵ֥ה אֱדֽוֹם

verses.restored: He commanded them, saying, Thus you shall say to my lord Esau: Thus says your servant Jacob, I have sojourned with Laban and stayed until now.

familiar.text: And he commanded them, saying, Thus shall ye speak unto my lord Esau...

modern.text: He instructed them, “You are to say to my master Esau, ‘Your servant Jacob says: I have been staying with Laban and have remained there until now.

original.text: וַיְצַ֤ו אֹתָם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר כֹּ֣ה תֹאמְר֔וּן לַֽאדֹנִ֖י לְעֵשָׂ֑ו כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ עַבְדְּךָ֣ יַעֲקֹ֔ב עִם לָבָ֣ן גַּ֔רְתִּי וָאֵחַ֖ר עַד עָֽתָּה

verses.restored: I have oxen, donkeys, flocks, male servants, and female servants, and I have sent to tell my lord, to find favor in your eyes.

familiar.text: And I have oxen, and asses, flocks, and menservants...

modern.text: I have oxen, donkeys, flocks, menservants, and maidservants. I have sent this message to inform my master, so that I may find favor in your sight.’”

original.text: וַֽיְהִי לִי֙ שׁ֣וֹר וַחֲמ֔וֹר צֹ֖אן וְעֶ֣בֶד וְשִׁפְחָ֑ה וָֽאֶשְׁלְחָה֙ לְהַגִּ֣יד לַֽאדֹנִ֔י לִמְצֹא חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: The messengers returned to Jacob, saying, We came to your brother Esau, and he is also coming to meet you, with four hundred men with him.

familiar.text: And the messengers returned to Jacob, saying, We came to thy brother Esau...

modern.text: When the messengers returned to Jacob, they said, “We went to your brother Esau, and now he is coming to meet you—he and four hundred men with him.”

original.text: וַיָּשֻׁ֨בוּ֙ הַמַּלְאָכִ֔ים אֶֽל יַעֲקֹ֖ב לֵאמֹ֑ר בָּ֤אנוּ אֶל אָחִ֨יךָ֙ אֶל עֵשָׂ֔ו וְגַם֙ הֹלֵ֣ךְ לִקְרָֽאתְךָ֔ וְאַרְבַּע מֵא֥וֹת אִ֖ישׁ עִמּֽוֹ

verses.restored: Jacob was very afraid and distressed. He divided the people who were with him, the flocks, herds, and camels, into two camps.

familiar.text: Then Jacob was greatly afraid and distressed...

modern.text: In great fear and distress, Jacob divided his people into two camps, as well as the flocks and herds and camels.

original.text: וַיִּירָ֧א יַעֲקֹ֛ב מְאֹ֖ד וַיֵּ֣צֶר ל֑וֹ וַיַּ֜חַץ אֶת הָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר אִתּ֗וֹ וְאֶת הַצֹּ֧אן וְאֶת הַבָּקָ֛ר וְהַגְּמַלִּ֖ים לִשְׁנֵ֥י מַחֲנֽוֹת

verses.restored: He said, If Esau comes to the one camp and strikes it, then the remaining camp will escape.

familiar.text: And said, If Esau come to the one company, and smite it...

modern.text: He thought, “If Esau comes and attacks one camp, then the other camp can escape.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אִם יָב֥וֹא עֵשָׂ֛ו אֶל הַמַּחֲנֶ֥ה הָאַחַ֖ת וְהִכָּ֑הוּ וְהָיָ֛ה הַמַּחֲנֶ֥ה הַנִּשְׁאָ֖ר לִפְלֵיטָֽה

verses.restored: Jacob said, Divine of my father Abraham and Divine of my father Isaac, Eternal, who said to me, Return to your land and to your kindred, and I will do good with you,

familiar.text: And Jacob said, O God of my father Abraham, and God of my father Isaac...

notes.title: Prayer of return
notes.body: Jacob prays by recalling the return command and promise.

modern.text: Then Jacob declared, “O God of my father Abraham, God of my father Isaac, the LORD who told me, ‘Go back to your country and to your kindred, and I will make you prosper,’

original.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֮ יַעֲקֹב֒ אֱלֹהֵי֙ אָבִ֣י אַבְרָהָ֔ם וֵאלֹהֵ֖י אָבִ֣י יִצְחָ֑ק יְהוָ֞ה הָאֹמֵ֣ר אֵלַ֗י שׁ֧וּב לְאַרְצְךָ֛ וּלְמוֹלַדְתְּךָ֖ וְאֵיטִ֥יבָה עִמָּֽךְ

verses.restored: I am too small for all the covenant-kindnesses and all the truth that you have done with your servant. With my staff I crossed this Jordan, and now I have become two camps.

familiar.text: I am not worthy of the least of all the mercies...

notes.title: Too small
notes.body: Jacob confesses humility before chesed and emet, loyal kindness and truth.

modern.text: I am unworthy of all the kindness and faithfulness You have shown Your servant. Indeed, with only my staff I came across the Jordan, but now I have become two camps.

original.text: קָטֹ֜נְתִּי מִכֹּ֤ל הַחֲסָדִים֙ וּמִכָּל הָ֣אֱמֶ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֖יתָ אֶת עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ כִּ֣י בְמַקְלִ֗י עָבַ֨רְתִּי֙ אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּ֣ן הַזֶּ֔ה וְעַתָּ֥ה הָיִ֖יתִי לִשְׁנֵ֥י מַחֲנֽוֹת

verses.restored: Please rescue me from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau, for I fear him, lest he come and strike me, mother upon children.

familiar.text: Deliver me, I pray thee, from the hand of my brother...

modern.text: Please deliver me from the hand of my brother Esau, for I am afraid that he may come and attack me and the mothers and children with me.

original.text: הַצִּילֵ֥נִי נָ֛א מִיַּ֥ד אָחִ֖י מִיַּ֣ד עֵשָׂ֑ו כִּֽי יָרֵ֤א אָנֹכִי֙ אֹת֔וֹ פֶּן יָב֣וֹא וְהִכַּ֔נִי אֵ֖ם עַל בָּנִֽים

verses.restored: But you said, I will surely do good with you and make your seed like the sand of the sea, which cannot be counted for multitude.

familiar.text: And thou saidst, I will surely do thee good...

modern.text: But You have said, ‘I will surely make you prosper, and I will make your offspring like the sand of the sea, too numerous to count.’”

original.text: וְאַתָּ֣ה אָמַ֔רְתָּ הֵיטֵ֥ב אֵיטִ֖יב עִמָּ֑ךְ וְשַׂמְתִּ֤י אֶֽת זַרְעֲךָ֙ כְּח֣וֹל הַיָּ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא יִסָּפֵ֖ר מֵרֹֽב

verses.restored: He spent that night there, and from what came into his hand he took a gift for Esau his brother:

familiar.text: And he lodged there that same night; and took of that which came to his hand...

modern.text: Jacob spent the night there, and from what he had brought with him, he selected a gift for his brother Esau:

original.text: וַיָּ֥לֶן שָׁ֖ם בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַה֑וּא וַיִּקַּ֞ח מִן הַבָּ֧א בְיָד֛וֹ מִנְחָ֖ה לְעֵשָׂ֥ו אָחִֽיו

verses.restored: two hundred female goats and twenty male goats, two hundred ewes and twenty rams,

familiar.text: Two hundred she goats, and twenty he goats...

modern.text: 200 female goats, 20 male goats, 200 ewes, 20 rams,

original.text: עִזִּ֣ים מָאתַ֔יִם וּתְיָשִׁ֖ים עֶשְׂרִ֑ים רְחֵלִ֥ים מָאתַ֖יִם וְאֵילִ֥ים עֶשְׂרִֽים

verses.restored: thirty nursing camels with their young, forty cows and ten bulls, twenty female donkeys and ten male donkeys.

familiar.text: Thirty milch camels with their colts, forty kine...

modern.text: 30 milk camels with their young, 40 cows, 10 bulls, 20 female donkeys, and 10 male donkeys.

original.text: גְּמַלִּ֧ים מֵינִיק֛וֹת וּבְנֵיהֶ֖ם שְׁלֹשִׁ֑ים פָּר֤וֹת אַרְבָּעִים֙ וּפָרִ֣ים עֲשָׂרָ֔ה אֲתֹנֹ֣ת עֶשְׂרִ֔ים וַעְיָרִ֖ם עֲשָׂרָֽה

verses.restored: He gave them into the hand of his servants, drove by drove, and said to his servants, Pass over before me, and put space between drove and drove.

familiar.text: And he delivered them into the hand of his servants, every drove by themselves...

modern.text: He entrusted them to his servants in separate herds and told them, “Go on ahead of me, and keep some distance between the herds.”

original.text: וַיִּתֵּן֙ בְּיַד עֲבָדָ֔יו עֵ֥דֶר עֵ֖דֶר לְבַדּ֑וֹ וַ֤יֹּאמֶר אֶל עֲבָדָיו֙ עִבְר֣וּ לְפָנַ֔י וְרֶ֣וַח תָּשִׂ֔ימוּ בֵּ֥ין עֵ֖דֶר וּבֵ֥ין עֵֽדֶר

verses.restored: He commanded the first, saying, When Esau my brother meets you and asks you, saying, Whose are you? Where are you going? Whose are these before you?

familiar.text: And he commanded the foremost, saying, When Esau my brother meeteth thee...

modern.text: He instructed the one in the lead, “When my brother Esau meets you and asks, ‘To whom do you belong, where are you going, and whose animals are these before you?’

original.text: וַיְצַ֥ו אֶת הָרִאשׁ֖וֹן לֵאמֹ֑ר כִּ֣י יִֽפְגָּשְׁךָ֞ עֵשָׂ֣ו אָחִ֗י וִשְׁאֵֽלְךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לְמִי אַ֨תָּה֙ וְאָ֣נָה תֵלֵ֔ךְ וּלְמִ֖י אֵ֥לֶּה לְפָנֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: then you shall say, They belong to your servant Jacob. It is a gift sent to my lord Esau, and look, he also is behind us.

familiar.text: Then thou shalt say, They be thy servant Jacob's...

modern.text: then you are to say, ‘They belong to your servant Jacob. They are a gift, sent to my lord Esau. And behold, Jacob is behind us.’”

original.text: וְאָֽמַרְתָּ֙ לְעַבְדְּךָ֣ לְיַעֲקֹ֔ב מִנְחָ֥ה הִוא֙ שְׁלוּחָ֔ה לַֽאדֹנִ֖י לְעֵשָׂ֑ו וְהִנֵּ֥ה גַם ה֖וּא אַחֲרֵֽינוּ

verses.restored: He commanded the second and the third and all who followed the droves, saying, In this way you shall speak to Esau when you find him,

familiar.text: And so commanded he the second, and the third...

modern.text: He also instructed the second, the third, and all those following behind the herds: “When you meet Esau, you are to say the same thing to him.

original.text: וַיְצַ֞ו גַּ֣ם אֶת הַשֵּׁנִ֗י גַּ֚ם אֶת הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֔י גַּ֚ם אֶת כָּל הַהֹ֣לְכִ֔ים אַחֲרֵ֥י הָעֲדָרִ֖ים לֵאמֹ֑ר כַּדָּבָ֤ר הַזֶּה֙ תְּדַבְּר֣וּן אֶל עֵשָׂ֔ו בְּמֹצַאֲכֶ֖ם אֹתֽוֹ

verses.restored: and you shall say, Also your servant Jacob is behind us. For he said, I will cover his face with the gift that goes before my face; afterward I will see his face. Perhaps he will lift my face.

familiar.text: And say ye moreover, Behold, thy servant Jacob is behind us...

notes.title: Face language
notes.body: Jacob’s gift strategy is full of face-language: cover face, see face, lift face. Reconciliation is embodied in the face.

modern.text: You are also to say, ‘Look, your servant Jacob is right behind us.’” For he thought, “I will appease Esau with the gift that is going before me. After that I can face him, and perhaps he will accept me. ”

original.text: וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֕ם גַּ֗ם הִנֵּ֛ה עַבְדְּךָ֥ יַעֲקֹ֖ב אַחֲרֵ֑ינוּ כִּֽי אָמַ֞ר אֲכַפְּרָ֣ה פָנָ֗יו בַּמִּנְחָה֙ הַהֹלֶ֣כֶת לְפָנָ֔י וְאַחֲרֵי כֵן֙ אֶרְאֶ֣ה פָנָ֔יו אוּלַ֖י יִשָּׂ֥א פָנָֽי

verses.restored: So the gift passed over before his face, while he spent that night in the camp.

familiar.text: So went the present over before him: and himself lodged that night...

modern.text: So Jacob’s gifts went on before him, while he spent the night in the camp. Jacob Wrestles with God

original.text: וַתַּעֲבֹ֥ר הַמִּנְחָ֖ה עַל פָּנָ֑יו וְה֛וּא לָ֥ן בַּלַּֽיְלָה הַה֖וּא בַּֽמַּחֲנֶֽה

verses.restored: He rose that night, took his two women, his two slave-women, and his eleven children, and crossed the ford of Jabbok.

familiar.text: And he rose up that night, and took his two wives...

modern.text: During the night Jacob got up and took his two wives, his two maidservants, and his eleven sons, and crossed the ford of the Jabbok.

original.text: וַיָּ֣קָם בַּלַּ֣יְלָה ה֗וּא וַיִּקַּ֞ח אֶת שְׁתֵּ֤י נָשָׁיו֙ וְאֶת שְׁתֵּ֣י שִׁפְחֹתָ֔יו וְאֶת אַחַ֥ד עָשָׂ֖ר יְלָדָ֑יו וַֽיַּעֲבֹ֔ר אֵ֖ת מַעֲבַ֥ר יַבֹּֽק

verses.restored: He took them and sent them across the stream, and sent across what belonged to him.

familiar.text: And he took them, and sent them over the brook...

modern.text: He took them and sent them across the stream, along with all his possessions.

original.text: וַיִּקָּחֵ֔ם וַיַּֽעֲבִרֵ֖ם אֶת הַנָּ֑חַל וַֽיַּעֲבֵ֖ר אֶת אֲשֶׁר לוֹ

verses.restored: Jacob was left alone, and a man wrestled with him until the rising of the dawn.

familiar.text: And Jacob was left alone; and there wrestled a man with him...

notes.title: Wrestled
notes.body: The verb yeaveq sounds like Jabbok and Jacob, binding name, place, and struggle.

modern.text: So Jacob was left all alone, and there a man wrestled with him until daybreak.

original.text: וַיִּוָּתֵ֥ר יַעֲקֹ֖ב לְבַדּ֑וֹ וַיֵּאָבֵ֥ק אִישׁ֙ עִמּ֔וֹ עַ֖ד עֲל֥וֹת הַשָּֽׁחַר

verses.restored: When he saw that he did not prevail against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh, and the hollow of Jacob’s thigh was dislocated as he wrestled with him.

familiar.text: And when he saw that he prevailed not against him, he touched the hollow...

modern.text: When the man saw that he could not overpower Jacob, he struck the socket of Jacob’s hip and dislocated it as they wrestled.

original.text: וַיַּ֗רְא כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יָכֹל֙ ל֔וֹ וַיִּגַּ֖ע בְּכַף יְרֵכ֑וֹ וַתֵּ֨קַע֙ כַּף יֶ֣רֶךְ יַעֲקֹ֔ב בְּהֵֽאָבְק֖וֹ עִמּֽוֹ

verses.restored: He said, Send me away, for the dawn has risen. He said, I will not send you away unless you bless me.

familiar.text: And he said, Let me go, for the day breaketh...

modern.text: Then the man said, “Let me go, for it is daybreak.” But Jacob replied, “I will not let you go unless you bless me.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שַׁלְּחֵ֔נִי כִּ֥י עָלָ֖ה הַשָּׁ֑חַר וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לֹ֣א אֲשַֽׁלֵּחֲךָ֔ כִּ֖י אִם בֵּרַכְתָּֽנִי

verses.restored: He said to him, What is your name? He said, Jacob.

familiar.text: And he said unto him, What is thy name? And he said, Jacob.

notes.title: Name confession
notes.body: Jacob must say his name before receiving the new name.

modern.text: “What is your name?” the man asked. “Jacob,” he replied.

original.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֵלָ֖יו מַה שְּׁמֶ֑ךָ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר יַעֲקֹֽב

verses.restored: He said, Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel, for you have struggled with the Divine and with humans, and you have prevailed.

familiar.text: And he said, Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel...

notes.title: Israel
notes.body: Israel is explained here through struggling with God/the Divine and humans and prevailing.

modern.text: Then the man said, “Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel, because you have struggled with God and with men, and you have prevailed.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לֹ֤א יַעֲקֹב֙ יֵאָמֵ֥ר עוֹד֙ שִׁמְךָ֔ כִּ֖י אִם יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּֽי שָׂרִ֧יתָ עִם אֱלֹהִ֛ים וְעִם אֲנָשִׁ֖ים וַתּוּכָֽל

verses.restored: Jacob asked and said, Please tell me your name. He said, Why is this that you ask my name? And he blessed him there.

familiar.text: And Jacob asked him, and said, Tell me, I pray thee, thy name...

modern.text: And Jacob requested, “Please tell me your name.” But he replied, “Why do you ask my name?” Then he blessed Jacob there.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁאַ֣ל יַעֲקֹ֗ב וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הַגִּֽידָה נָּ֣א שְׁמֶ֔ךָ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לָ֥מָּה זֶּ֖ה תִּשְׁאַ֣ל לִשְׁמִ֑י וַיְבָ֥רֶךְ אֹת֖וֹ שָֽׁם

verses.restored: Jacob called the name of the place Peniel, for I have seen the Divine face to face, and my life has been rescued.

familiar.text: And Jacob called the name of the place Peniel: for I have seen God face to face...

notes.title: Peniel
notes.body: Peniel means face of God/the Divine. The face theme continues from Jacob’s fear of Esau’s face.

modern.text: So Jacob named the place Peniel, saying, “Indeed, I have seen God face to face, and yet my life was spared.”

original.text: וַיִּקְרָ֧א יַעֲקֹ֛ב שֵׁ֥ם הַמָּק֖וֹם פְּנִיאֵ֑ל כִּֽי רָאִ֤יתִי אֱלֹהִים֙ פָּנִ֣ים אֶל פָּנִ֔ים וַתִּנָּצֵ֖ל נַפְשִֽׁי

verses.restored: The sun rose upon him as he passed Penuel, and he was limping because of his thigh.

familiar.text: And as he passed over Penuel the sun rose upon him, and he halted upon his thigh.

modern.text: The sun rose above him as he passed by Penuel, and he was limping because of his hip.

original.text: וַיִּֽזְרַֽח ל֣וֹ הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָבַ֖ר אֶת פְּנוּאֵ֑ל וְה֥וּא צֹלֵ֖עַ עַל יְרֵכֽוֹ

verses.restored: Therefore the sons of Israel do not eat the sinew of the hip that is on the hollow of the thigh to this day, because he touched the hollow of Jacob’s thigh at the sinew of the hip.

familiar.text: Therefore the children of Israel eat not of the sinew which shrank...

modern.text: Therefore to this day the Israelites do not eat the tendon which is at the socket of the hip, because the socket of Jacob’s hip was struck near that tendon.

original.text: עַל כֵּ֡ן לֹֽא יֹאכְל֨וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶת גִּ֣יד הַנָּשֶׁ֗ה אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל כַּ֣ף הַיָּרֵ֔ךְ עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה כִּ֤י נָגַע֙ בְּכַף יֶ֣רֶךְ יַעֲקֹ֔ב בְּגִ֖יד הַנָּשֶֽׁה
